question: Does the CR120Z B-then-X1 order discriminator survive finite-shot tomography under the three frozen CR223c high-fidelity NV noise profiles and matched resource controls?
profiles: Import exact room_temp_NV, cryogenic_NV, and noisy_NV parameters from CR223c_HF_summary.json

simulation.state_estimator: two-qubit Pauli linear inversion followed by PSD projection and trace normalization
simulation.readout_correction: invert the frozen symmetric bit-flip attenuation per Pauli weight

noise_mapping.SPAM: mix input with I4/4 at profile spam_err
noise_mapping.pulse_error: global depolarization after each of two matched stages
noise_mapping.phase_noise: blockwise Rz error on the B request stage
noise_mapping.drift: blockwise correlated ZZ phase-flip probability capped below 1/4
noise_mapping.readout: symmetric observable attenuation and frozen inverse correction

validation_gates: all source and seal hashes match
all reconstructed states are PSD and unit trace
known Bell and product calibration states remain distinguishable in all profiles
forward median negativity exceeds 0.30 in every profile
forward 5th-percentile negativity exceeds every direct-control 95th percentile by at least 0.15 in every profile
matched forward-minus-reverse negativity gap is positive in at least 47 of 48 validation blocks per profile
forward median frozen-setting CHSH exceeds 2.30 and at least 45 of 48 blocks exceed 2 in every profile
resolved Bell-response swapping survives with 5th-percentile negativity above 0.20 while product and unresolved controls stay below 0.05 at their 95th percentiles
local marginals remain invariant in the exact noisy channel within 1e-12
all semantic and statistical wrong controls are rejected
forbidden_claims: a simulator result installs a SAM operator
finite-shot survival proves a physical B/X1 weld
